title: Finite two-block harmonic coarse Schur assembly
question: Does retaining the two block-constant modes and eliminating the R-422 residual by harmonic extension yield a positive finite coarse Schur and combined lower envelope on the fixed Q3 grid?

new_perspective.principle: Do not discard the two block-constant modes when the residual reserve is assembled. Use the exact finite harmonic Schur complement for the block-constant coordinates and reuse the independently checked residual form on its orthogonal complement.
route: Keep the R-419 conditional Gibbs law, projected momentum conductance, beta grid, orientations, alpha=1/40 and tail threshold theta=4 unchanged.
For every eligible R-422 core/tail row, construct the weighted block-constant span and its Euclidean orthogonal block-mean-zero complement after the sqrt(pi) transform.
Use R-406 harmonic extension to compute the coarse Schur gap, residual gap and exact energy/variance decomposition.
Independently recompute the block-mean-zero residual eigenvalue using the R-422 basis and require agreement within the declared comparison tolerance.
Record the conservative finite combined lower envelope 0.5*min(coarse gap,residual gap) without clipping or promoting nonuniform constants.
new_perspective.qft_bridge: The finite assembly identifies the remaining analytic target: a common-core estimate must control both the coarse Schur sector and the residual sector with constants that survive cutoff, volume, phase and exhaustion limits.

finite_theorem.space: The centered finite weighted graph is decomposed into the two-dimensional block-constant span U and the block-mean-zero complement V after the sqrt(pi) transform.
finite_theorem.harmonic_schur: For z in U, the residual coordinate y=-A_VV^(-1)A_VU z minimizes the finite Dirichlet form and produces S=A_UU-A_UV A_VV^(-1)A_VU.
finite_theorem.coarse_gap: The first positive generalized eigenvalue of the Schur form relative to the harmonic coarse mass is the finite coarse Schur gap.
finite_theorem.residual_gap: The least eigenvalue of A_VV is the finite block-mean-zero residual gap.
finite_theorem.combined_lower_envelope: The exact harmonic/residual energy and variance split yields the conservative centered lower envelope 0.5*min(coarse_gap,residual_gap) for the declared finite probes and decomposition.
finite_theorem.scope_boundary: This is a row-by-row finite matrix assembly. It does not identify U or V with a physical sector, a common Hamiltonian form domain, or a regulator-independent limit.

lean_crosscheck.boundary: Lean checks scalar harmonic split and lower-envelope algebra only; it does not formalize the Q3 matrix eigensolver, Gibbs rows, Schur spectra, common core or any limit.

assumptions: The R-419 conditional law is positive and normalized and the projected conductance is symmetric and nonnegative.
The R-422 core/tail split is reused exactly with no row-dependent retuning of alpha or theta.
The sqrt(pi) transform preserves the finite weighted Dirichlet form and the block basis is formed from disjoint nonempty supports.
The residual block A_VV is positive on every eligible finite row, so the harmonic solve is well-defined.
The finite harmonic split is evaluated without rounding lower bounds upward, and the Lean lane is a scalar cross-check rather than a matrix formalization.
missing_assumptions: A cutoff-, volume-, phase- and exhaustion-uniform lower bound for both the coarse Schur and residual forms on one Hamiltonian common core.
A common split-limit map controlling the block-constant variables and residual coordinates under changing regulators and volumes.
Two-sided form-norm control of actual R-399 histories and a transfer theorem through the R-415 semigroup estimates.
Hamiltonian-to-OS/KMS/GNS identification and a sectorwise coercive estimate.
promotion_criteria: Prove an analytic Schur/residual decomposition on a domain-controlled unbounded Q3 common core.
Establish a positive lower envelope uniform in cutoff, volume, phase and exhaustion, including the coarse Schur sector.
Transfer the bound through the declared history and semigroup interfaces before revisiting any sector or physical promotion.
stop_conditions: A singular residual block, nonpositive coarse Schur gap or disagreement with the independent residual recomputation stops the lane and is recorded as a finite construction failure.
A nonpositive finite lower envelope is retained as a sufficient-budget failure and is not clipped, relabeled or used as a gapless conclusion.
Finite harmonic Schur positivity cannot be promoted to global Poincare, OS/KMS/GNS, C6, Sector-A, Pre-A, Yang-Mills or mass-gap closure.
evidence_level: T0 / exact finite harmonic coarse-Schur decomposition plus executed Q3-row assembly; no uniform theorem or physical conclusion
non_claims: No cutoff-, volume-, phase- or exhaustion-uniform coarse or residual bound.
No global Poincare or arbitrary-observable Schur theorem.
No common Hamiltonian core, common split rule or history transfer.
No OS/KMS/GNS reconstruction or sectorwise spectral gap.
No continuum, C6, Sector-A, Pre-A, Yang-Mills or mass-gap conclusion.

formal_integration.event_title: R-424 finite two-block harmonic coarse Schur assembly
formal_integration.lean: R424 PASS; scalar harmonic split and lower-envelope algebra only

boundary: R-424 closes only the finite two-block harmonic Schur assembly and its residual reuse on the fixed Q3 grid. It does not close the Q3LOCK common-alpha or broken-sector coercivity parent gates.
next_unlock: Obtain a domain-controlled analytic estimate for the coarse Schur capacity and residual boundary budget that is uniform in the regulator and then transfer it through the history/OS/KMS/GNS interfaces.
no_overclaim: A positive finite combined lower envelope is a conditional matrix-level certificate. It is not a regulator-independent phase gap, a physical-vacuum statement, a Yang-Mills result or a mass gap.
